description: The young commander of the 30th Division of the Demon Slayers, the Order of Light. Joshua is the youngest man to ever become commander in the history of Akras Summoners' Hall. He accrued so many accomplishments during his rookie years that it proved impossible to keep track of all them. The day he was assigned to a certain Demon Slayers' reconnaissance mission and returned to headquarters having slayed the demon all by himself, not even Elder Summoner Karl could hide his amazement. Although his skill cannot be denied, his rash behavior and abrasive manner of speaking tend to isolate him from everyone else.After being made commander, he successfully completed even more crucial missions one after another. No matter how difficult the situation is, Joshua always manages to overcome it in his own way. He garnered the respect of those around him, who dubbed him "Joshua of Sanjelo". So far none of the other young Summoners in Summoners' Hall have been able to prove themselves his equal, and thus he is being highly considered for a position as a Summoner of Old in the near future.When a mysterious military force began its attack, Joshua was called back from a mission in the dangerous and demon-ridden land of Ishgria. He rushed into the scene and ambushed its commander, effectively stopping their invasion on the Imperial Capital. Joshua continued to fell foe after foe in his own independent and rash way, and although this caused quite the headache for the Summoners of Old from time to time, he was forgiven because he always yields the desired resilts. There is no one who can deny that Joshua's skill is the best display of power that Akras Summoners' Hall has to offer.
summon: I've been waiting for you.Let's go, I'll protect you.After all, that was the mission assigned to me.
fusion: One should focus their power on a single point, then strike with all their might.It seems your mind works the same way.Good. Keep it up.
evolution: Many admire Elder Summoner Karl.I guess even innate talent cannot flourish without experience.There's still much to learn from him.
